IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.    OF 2026
[arising out of SLP (C) No  11692/2024]
CHANDRA MOHAN LINGAM                               Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
SUDHA & ANR.                                       Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The present appeal is arising out of order dated 28.11.2023
passed by the High Court of Karnataka at Dharwad Bench in MFA No.
101433/2020.
3. The facts of the case reveal that an accident took place on
17.06.2015 around 07:45 pm and the appellant before this court
suffered serious injuries.
4. At the time of accident, he was aged about 50 years and
working as Architect. A Claim Petition was preferred and the Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) granted compensation for a total
sum of Rs. 7,65,600/- (Rs. Seven Lakh Sixty Five Thousand and Six
Hundred only). The appellant who is an Architect preferred an
appeal before the High court stating that he has lost his one eye,
he is 60% disabled and being an Architect now he cannot work on
site and therefore, the amount be enhanced.
5. The High Court enhanced the amount after hearing parties at
length, totaling to Rs. 15,28,002/- (Rs. Fifteen Lakh Twenty Eight
thousand and Two only). The amount of compensation has been
received by the appellant.

## Page 198

2
5. Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently argued before
this Court that an Architect who has lost his eye and who has 60%
physical disability, is not in a position to work properly. He is
not able to attend construction sites and therefore, under the head
“Loss of earning capacity”, the amount granted by the High Court
and the MACT is too meager. He has also stated that that his income
was not taken into account rightly though ITRs are placed on record
and he has claimed further enhancement under various heads.
6. On the other hand learned counsel for the Insurance Company
vehemently opposed the prayer for enhancement of compensation. He
has argued before this Court that loss of eye was not on account of
accident but in fact the appellant was suffering from diabetes and
on account of diabetes, he lost his eye. Though he has not disputed
the 60% disability in the lower limb. He has stated that the MACT
has rightly awarded the compensation which was right enhanced by
the High Court and the scope for further enhancement does not
arise.
7. This  court  has  carefully  gone  through  the  disability
certificate, the ITRs and the amount under various heads by the
High Court. The High Court has awarded Rs. 9,25,002/- to the
petitioner under head of “Loss of earning capacity”. Only Rs.
50,000/- has been awarded for the further amenities of life.
8. In the considered opinion of this Court, the interest of
justice would be served by enhancing the compensation in exercise
of powers conferred under Article 142 of the Constitution of India
further by a sum of Rs. 10,00,000/- (Rs. Ten Lakh only).
9. The amount shall be paid by the Insurance Company within a

## Page 199

3
period of six weeks from today failing which it will carry interest
@ 9% per annum.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant shall furnish details of the
account within a period of one week to learned counsel for the
Insurance Company enabling him to transmit the amount directly in
the account of the petitioner.
11. With the aforesaid, the Civil Appeal is allowed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
…………………………………………………………………. J.

In such circumstances, we deem it appropriate to affirm
the  interim  relief  granted  earlier  subject  to  the
following three conditions:

investigation  and  make  himself  available  for
interrogation as and when required by the investigating
agency;

bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court

(iii)  The  amount  of  Rs.12  lakhs  deposited  in  the
Registry of this Court shall along with interest, if
any, be transmitted to the Court of Session, Fatehabad
(State of Haryana).

1 impugned judgment
1

## Page 221

2. In compliance with the order passed by this Court yesterday, the Registrar
General of the High Court of Madras has furnished to this Court the uploaded
copy of the impugned judgment. 
3. It appears that the impugned judgment and order was uploaded only
yesterday, around 16.40 hours. It requires no special intelligence to infer that
but for the intervention of this Court, the impugned judgment would not have
been uploaded yesterday at all.
4. Be that as it may, having perused the impugned judgment, this Court
finds  no  reason  to  interfere  therewith;  hence,  the  special  leave  petition  is
dismissed.
5. Petitioner is, however, left free to pursue the channel of civil litigation or
other  remedy  in  accordance  with  law.  Any  proceeding  instituted  by  the
petitioner may be considered on its own merits without being influenced by any
observation made in the impugned judgment or dismissal of this special leave
petition. 
6. Connected application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of. 
7. Before  parting,  this  Court  would  remind  Hon’ble  Judges  to consider a
mechanism for timely uploading of judgments/orders notwithstanding the heavy
burden of judicial work that each Hon’ble Judge of a high court has to bear.
After all, the right to a reasoned order is illusory if the judgment/order itself is
not made available to the litigant who might seek to challenge it before a higher
court.  The  delay  in  uploading,  though  unintentional,  could  cause  serious
prejudice to him/it. That apart, omission/neglect to upload any judgment or
order within a reasonable period and not uploading it for more than six weeks,
as  in  this  case,  raises  unnecessary  doubts  and  could  lead  to  unforeseen
2

## Page 222

complications as well as undesirable criticism which should best be avoided by
ensuring timely availability thereof. This Court trusts that this shall not recur
and that judgments/orders shall be made available to the litigants promptly.

alia, pointing out that an inquiry was made at the Sri Sri Thakur
1

## Page 227

Anukulchandra Satsang Ashram, Deoghar, where no entry of Mr. Burman
or any Bangladeshi national on 24/25.03.2025 was found. The ashram
employee informed that foreign visitors are required to request
accommodation by way of an email and no such email was received
from him. The State of Jharkhand has, accordingly, advised the
petitioner No. 1 to lodge an FIR regarding the missing person along
with his photograph, mobile number, etc., so that the necessary
investigation can be done. 
2. Similarly, the State of West Bengal has also filed a status
report, inter alia, pointing out that Mr. Burman entered India on
20.03.2025 through Fulbari Integrated Check Post on a medical visa
valid till 18.07.2025 for treatment at Star Hospital, Siliguri. He
attended the OPD on 21.03.2024 and 22.03.2025 but was never
admitted to the hospital. There is also no record of any later
visits. The status report further clarifies that he was neither
apprehended/detained nor questioned by the New Jalpaiguri Police
Station and no FIR was registered. The CDR analysis of his mobile
number, which he obtained locally on his passport, showed that he
stayed  at  Shiv  Mandir,  Matigara  on  the  nights  between  20-
22.03.2025, and travelled via Purnia and Bhagalpur on 23.03.2025.
The said mobile was active near the aforementioned Satsang Ashram
in Deoghar on a particular date and time, but his whereabouts
thereafter are not known. The mobile handset was subsequently used
with another SIM card by one Shambhu Kumar Yadav of Katoria, Banka,
Bihar, whose telephonic explanation was found inconclusive. 
3. Accordingly, we direct the Union of India to file a status
report with specific reference to the communication received from

the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Bangladesh (Annexure
P.5). 
4. In the meantime, petitioner No. 1, if so advised, may get an
FIR registered.

Court at Munger District, Bihar to the Court of Principal Judge,

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, we are not
inclined to interfere with the impugned order(s) which is well within the four
corners of Order XXI Rule 42 of the CPC.
1

## Page 324

3. Be that as it may. The primary grievance of the petitioner is that the appeal
filed against the order of eviction is not being heard. Even according to the
petitioner, undisputedly, the appeal is defective. If it is so, the Registry shall not
insist for the physical presence of the petitioner for curing the defect, who is
said  to  be  in  judicial  custody.  Hence,  we  permit  the  learned  advocate
representing appellant/petitioner to cure the defects, if any. In the event of any
rule  mandates  her  physical  appearance,  for  instance,  the  petitioner  having
presented the appeal as an indigent person and his/her statement under oath is
required to be obtained, then in such circumstances, the applicant cannot be
permitted  to  contend  that  physical  appearance  would  not  be  necessary.
Otherwise, the learned advocate is permitted to rectify the defects pointed out
by the Registry and if the papers are in order, the appeal may be posted before
the jurisdictional court and thereafter it may be disposed of on merits and in
accordance with law.
4. With this observation, the Special Leave Petitions stand dismissed.
5.Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH & ORS.                     Respondent(s)
(FOR ADMISSION) 
(With I.A. No.339614/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.)
 
Date : 06-11-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DIPANKAR DATTA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SHEEL NAGU
For Petitioner(s)  Mr. Saurabh Mishra, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Ashutosh Kumar- 3241, AOR
                   
                   
For Respondent(s)  
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. By presenting this writ petition under Article 32 of the Constitution, the
petitioners pray the following relief:
“(a) issue a writ of mandamus, or any other appropriate writ, order or direction,
directing Respondent Nos. 1 and 3 to consider and determine, by a reasoned
order and within three months or such other time as this Hon’ble Court may fix,
whether  the  Samvida  Shala  Shikshak  Patrata  Pariksha  of  2005  and  2008,
conducted under the M.P. Panchayat/Nagariya Nikay Samvida Shala Shikshak
(Employment and Conditions of Contract) Rules, 2005, read with the training
qualification acquired by the Petitioners and their length of service, satisfies the
requirement of the Teacher Eligibility Test under Section 23(1) of the RTE Act
and the NCTE Notification dated 23.08.2010;
(b) direct that, in the event the examination is determined to be equivalent, the
Petitioners shall be treated on par with CTET-qualified teachers under para 3 of
Circular  No.  UCR/C/85/P.Pari./Pra.Shi./2026/1839  dated  17.09.2026  for  all
purposes, including continuance in service and promotion;
(c) direct that para 2 of the impugned Circular dated 17.09.2026 shall not be

## Page 520

2
enforced  against  the  Petitioners  pending  such  determination,  and  that  the
Petitioners’  non-application  for  the  examination  for  which  the  last  date  was
05.10.2026 shall not prejudice them in any manner; and
(d) pass such other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Court may deem fit and
proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.”
2. Mr. Mishra, learned senior counsel for the petitioners, has failed to invite
our attention to any provision of law imposing a duty on the respondents to
determine  the  question  of  equivalence  of  examinations  which  in-service
teachers like the petitioners claim to have qualified prior to introduction of the
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 with the Teachers
Eligibility Test prescribed by the National Council for Teacher Education under
Section 23 thereof. 
3. In our opinion, this writ petition is a device to circumvent the directions
given by this Court in  Anjuman Ishaat-e-Taleem Trust v. The State of
Maharashtra and Others1 (Civil Appeal No.1385 of 2025), since confirmed on
review in State of U.P. v. Anjuman Ishaat-e-Taleem Trust & Ors.2 [Review
Petition (C) Diary No.53434/2025 in Civil Appeal No.1385/2025], requiring in-
service teachers having more than 5 years’ service left to qualify the Teachers
Eligibility Test, in default, to make room for others.
4. Since this is a thoroughly misconceived writ petition, we dismiss the same
with costs of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh) only to be paid to the Supreme
Court Bar Clerks Association within a period of two months from date.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
